clue.text: In possession of Burma's king, tapestry that's put up for decoration

indicators.note: the run of words holds the letters inside them, as if keeping hold of the answer

explanation.surface: A hanging tapestry owned by a Burmese monarch is displayed as an ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In possession of' signals letters held inside BurMA'S KING TAPEstry.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorators stick this adhesive strip along edges before painting a room, so it is put up when decorating.

clue.text: A mild UN broadcast that gets half-cut?

definitions.note: half-cut is British slang for tipsy; the question mark admits the stretch to tearfully drunk

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so these letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A meek United Nations broadcast that leaves listeners a little tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges A MILD UN.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes the self-pitying, weepy sentimentality typical of someone who has been drinking.

clue.text: Bouquets creating impression when delivered

indicators.note: delivered as in spoken out, like a speech, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: an impression is a sense or feeling about something

explanation.surface: Flowers that make a good impression once handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when delivered' says the word for impression, SENSE, is heard; it sounds like SCENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its aroma, so bouquets are smells or perfumes.

clue.text: One with spoilt mentality personally

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: spoilt means ruined, so the word mentality is broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Someone with a pampered attitude, described in a personal way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoilt' is the anagram signal on the word mentality; I for one is the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something personally means doing it in a close, private, first-hand way.

clue.text: Open Jeep gang's taken over regularly

indicators.note: taken over suggests turning something over, so the picked letters run backwards
regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

explanation.surface: An open-topped Jeep is seized by a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes EPAG from jEeP gAnG's; 'taken over' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stand wide open, like a gaping wound or hole.

clue.text: He's active in the masses observed by the ministry, sometimes getting cross

definitions.text: He's active in the masses observed by the ministry, sometimes getting cross

parts.words: He's active in the masses observed by the ministry, sometimes getting cross
parts.note: a youngster who serves at Mass in church, watched by the clergy, and who at times carries the processional cross

explanation.surface: A political activist among the masses, watched by a government ministry, who sometimes loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The masses are church services, the ministry is the clergy, and getting cross means picking up the crucifix rather than losing his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: This lad assists the priest at Mass and may carry the cross in procession.

clue.text: Green with no well — financial resources needed

parts.note: eco- is the environmental prefix, as in eco-friendly
well and my are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: An environmental project with no water well needs funding.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation's economy is its wealth and the management of its money and goods.

clue.text: Most bitter requires little bit of money and relaxation

parts.note: a sou was an old French coin of tiny value
relaxation is rest

explanation.surface: Someone at their most resentful needs some cash and a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour and bitter are close tastes and moods; this is the superlative.

clue.text: Striker needs security before game

parts.note: security is safety
a game is a match

explanation.surface: A football striker needs protection before the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' looks like a footballer; it is something struck against a box.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of match lights only when struck on the special strip of its box, so it is a striker.

clue.text: Woeful poet I edited, American

indicators.note: edited text is reworked, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: US is short for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: A miserable American poet whose work I edited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges POET I into PITEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something pitiful that arouses sorrow or sympathy.

clue.text: Kent lose terribly important opening all-rounder?

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters of Kent lose are scrambled

parts.note: key means important, as in a key player

explanation.surface: Kent's cricket team badly loses its key opening all-rounder.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is an English county with a cricket team; an all-rounder bats and bowls, and an opener bats first. 'terribly' rearranges KENT LOSE into SKELETON.
explanation.definitionFit: This single key opens many different locks, so it is an opener that handles them all.

clue.text: End of tie seen at work every day

definitions.meaning: a tie is a match, and its final whistle comes at the close of play
describes a job of a whole working week rather than part of it

explanation.surface: Someone's necktie comes undone while they are at work every day.
explanation.walkthrough: A tie is a sporting fixture, such as a cup tie, not a necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the final whistle of a match and a job worked for complete standard hours.

clue.text: Hollow wood with nothing inside

indicators.note: inside places the nothing within the wood

parts.note: a grove is a small wood
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A hollow piece of timber with nothing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a long narrow channel or hollow cut into a surface.

clue.text: Sort of design a clue for 'Rat' in French?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer says take ART and make it new, which gives the clue's Rat; the new is said in French

explanation.surface: A style of design is offered as a clue for a French rat.
explanation.walkthrough: Nouveau is French for new, a common anagram signal, so the answer read as a clue makes RAT from ART; 'in French' explains the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the flowing, plant-inspired decorative style popular around 1900.

clue.text: Lean nurse

definitions.meaning: to lean towards something is to incline that way
to nurse is to look after or care for

explanation.surface: A thin nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to have an inclination and to look after someone.

clue.text: Cassette player perhaps found next to class pigeonhole

parts.note: a cassette player is one example of a stereo
a class is a type

explanation.surface: A tape deck sits beside a shelf compartment in a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To pigeonhole people is to put them in a fixed category by an oversimplified label.

clue.text: A compelling figure in orchestration, Gil Evans

indicators.note: orchestration arranges music, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Gil Evans, the jazz arranger, showed compelling presence in his orchestral arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: Gil Evans was a jazz arranger, which makes orchestration fit the surface. 'in orchestration' rearranges GIL EVANS.
explanation.definitionFit: In du Maurier's novel Trilby, this hypnotist controls a singer; the name now means anyone with a controlling hold.

clue.text: Mother fast to catch rodent — nasty!

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: catching something holds it within, so the fast surrounds the rodent

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
a vole is a small rodent

explanation.surface: A mother, quick to trap a rat, cries out in disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone who wishes harm on others.

clue.text: Fly-in mail, trend used off and on with restrictions

indicators.note: using letters off and on means taking every other one, skipping the rest

explanation.surface: A trend for airmail flown in is subject to limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used off and on' takes the even letters of fLyInMaIlTrEnD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with restrictions has bounds placed on it, such as a limited edition.

clue.text: Ring up over head displaying saintliness

definitions.text: Ring up over head displaying saintliness

parts.words: Ring up over head displaying saintliness
parts.note: a glowing circle shown above the head of a saint in paintings

explanation.surface: Phoning someone, then a hint about a saintly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring up' looks like making a phone call; it is a ring placed up above the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious art shows holy figures with a circle of light above or around their heads.

clue.text: A Roman way to run gets one flying

parts.note: via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A route along an old Roman road gets someone into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is someone who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Result: fine is doubled in East European court

indicators.note: in places the doubled letter within the letters for East European court

parts.note: E is the compass point east

indicators.note: doubled means the letter for fine appears twice

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: The outcome: a fine is doubled in an Eastern European court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is doubled' writes the fine letter twice and 'in' sets the pair after the first E, splitting East from European court.
explanation.definitionFit: An effect is the outcome or consequence of a cause.

clue.text: A comedian should have this hat I'm in, gran admits

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the phrase holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: A grandmother admits a comedian should wear the hat she is in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' signals the letters inside haT I'M IN Gran.
explanation.definitionFit: Comics depend on delivering punchlines at exactly the right moment.

clue.text: A gent may wear this belt and tie

parts.note: to belt someone is to hit them, to cuff them
a tie is a link or connection

explanation.surface: A gentleman may wear a belt and a necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' and 'tie' look like clothing; they are a blow and a connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman fastens shirt cuffs with this piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Irritable, being on the fringes?

definitions.meaning: irritable means tense and on edge
read as edge plus -y, of the edges, positioned at the border

explanation.surface: Someone tetchy because they live on the margins of society.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means nervy and tense, and playfully suggests something sitting at the edges.

clue.text: Panama usually has one marking its borders

definitions.text: Panama usually has one marking its borders

parts.words: Panama usually has one marking its borders
parts.note: a panama is a straw hat, normally with a ribbon round where crown meets brim

explanation.surface: The country of Panama usually has something marking its national borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' looks like the country; it is the straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: This ribbon circles the crown of a hat just above the brim.

clue.text: Visiting cathedral city, reportedly crashed with an upright carriage

indicators.note: visiting puts one thing within another, so the crashed sound goes inside the city

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: reportedly means by word of mouth, so we hear the word and write its sound

parts.note: a crashed car is wrecked

explanation.surface: A coach visiting a cathedral city is said to have crashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' is the sound signal on crashed, and 'Visiting' the container. 'carriage' looks like a vehicle; it is posture. Ely is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage here means bearing or posture, so moving with straight, upright posture.

clue.text: It's delivered along the ground air ducts, yet to be processed

indicators.note: processing turns raw material into something new, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Air ducts are delivered by the ground crew, not yet processed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the ball is delivered (bowled); this is a ball that skims along the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a ball bowled so low it rolls or skims along the turf earns this name.
